title: Active test selection: which 2 of 4 questions to ask about a hidden target
question: Given a table of 4 candidates, can the model learn to choose the 2 attribute queries that best discriminate between them (expected information gain), and so answer better than random questions at the same compute?

predictions.PASS: learned queries beat random queries by >= 10 points and come within 5 points of the exact expected-information-gain policy (same answer head)
predictions.A3: reported: the advantage holds on OOD tables where the separating pair uses attributes 3/4
predictions.design: three models with the same architecture, each trained AND evaluated with one query policy (learned, random, exact EIG), so every answer head matches its own query distribution. A local smoke test that evaluated one learned-policy model under all three policies was unfair to EIG (72 vs 52%) and was replaced before any run.

prior_art: Bayesian experimental design / expected information gain (Lindley 1956), BALD 1112.5745, active feature acquisition
not_claimed: Information-gain query selection is prior art; the question is whether a small model learns it end to end.
